lessonPlan.languageObjective: Learners understand and produce the target vocabulary (first name, last name, spell, phone number, numbers 1-20) and use the lesson pattern (How do you spell it?, What’s your phone number?, He/She is … years old.) with beginner-level accuracy.
lessonPlan.parentSuggestions: Ask the learner to explain or demonstrate one thing learned in the lesson without pressure.
lessonPlan.usefulExpressions: Key lesson expressions based on: How do you spell it?, What’s your phone number?, He/She is … years old.
lessonPlan.commonDifficulties: Limited vocabulary recall, hesitation, confusion about word order, pronunciation difficulty, or dependence on the model.
lessonPlan.suggestedSolutions: Use visuals, two-choice prompts, sentence frames, slowed modelling, choral repetition, one focused correction, and a final supported retry.
lessonPlan.formativeAssessment: Monitor comprehension, pronunciation, controlled practice, and response quality throughout the lesson.
lessonPlan.summativeAssessment: Use a short exit task requiring one understanding check and one target-language production.
lessonPlan.diagnosticAssessment: Begin with one quick recall or recognition prompt to identify prior knowledge.
lessonPlan.pedagogicalFramework: Warm-up → Presentation → Practice → Production → Assessment → Homework. Meaning comes before correction, and support is gradually removed.
lessonPlan.assessmentForLearning: Use observation, recognition checks, oral responses, controlled practice accuracy, self-correction, and one exit performance.
lessonPlan.communicativeObjective: Learners exchange simple information related to “Letters, Spelling and Numbers 1-20” through a guided dialogue, response task, or short personal production.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Hello!
lessons.label: Lesson 1
lessons.theme: Greetings, introductions, classroom language, and the alphabet

lessonPlanData.theme: Greetings, introductions, classroom language, and the alphabet

stages.assessment: Observe confidence, prior knowledge, and willingness to respond.
stages.studentActivities: Respond chorally and individually and share any greeting expressions already known.
stages.teacherActivities: Smile, wave, greet the class, elicit a choral response, greet several learners individually, and diagnose prior knowledge.

stages.assessment: Recognition questions and accurate repetition.
stages.studentActivities: Look, predict, listen, identify key phrases, tick answers, and repeat.
stages.teacherActivities: Present the greeting dialogue in context, ask learners to predict, model or play it, check phrases heard, and model pronunciation and intonation.

stages.assessment: Greeting, name, polite response, and intelligibility checklist.
stages.studentActivities: Practise using personal names, switch roles, and repeat with another partner.
stages.teacherActivities: Model the complete dialogue with one learner, assign repetitions, organise pairs, require role switching, and monitor gently.

stages.assessment: Correctly perform or identify at least four instructions.
stages.studentActivities: Watch, imitate, repeat, act, match, and respond physically.
stages.teacherActivities: Teach classroom verbs and instructions using action, gesture, written forms, and mixed-order commands.

stages.assessment: Accuracy, participation, and English use.
stages.studentActivities: Mime, guess, keep score, and take turns.
stages.teacherActivities: Model and organise a mime game in groups, ensure turn-taking, and monitor equal participation.

stages.assessment: Recognition, pronunciation, and accurate recording.
stages.studentActivities: Listen, repeat, complete sequences, say chosen letters, listen to a partner, and write.
stages.teacherActivities: Display the alphabet chart, model letter names, lead a rhythm task, guide missing-letter work, and model partner dictation.

stages.assessment: Four-part exit ticket and confidence note.
stages.studentActivities: Greet, say their name, follow one instruction, and say three letters.
stages.teacherActivities: Invite an independent mini-performance and administer the exit ticket.

lessonPlanData.grammar: Communicative chunks: I’m + name; My name is + name; Nice to meet you; Nice to meet you too.
lessonPlanData.grouping: Whole class, pairs, groups of 3–5, and individual performance.
lessonPlanData.homework: Practise the greeting dialogue with a family member and write five English alphabet letters.
lessonPlanData.outcomes: Learners participate in a short greeting dialogue, demonstrate classroom routines, match classroom verbs to visuals, and complete a basic alphabet task.
lessonPlanData.textbook: English Spotlight 1 — Student Book Part A
lessonPlanData.functions: Greeting; introducing oneself; responding politely; following classroom instructions.
lessonPlanData.resources: Student Book pages 7–10; greetings poster; classroom-language cards; instruction cards; alphabet chart; exit ticket; board.
lessonPlanData.sourceBook: English Spotlight 1 Student Book Part A
lessonPlanData.vocabulary: hello, hi, name, nice to meet you, listen, look, talk, speak, read, write, draw, match, point, stand up, sit down, open your book, close your book, raise your hand, work in pairs, work in groups
lessonPlanData.generatedBy: Happy Office Curriculum Engineering — Elvy Pedagogy Standards
lessonPlanData.teacherTips: Model every speaking task first, assign repetitions, switch roles and partners, use gestures consistently, avoid long grammar explanations, and keep the room emotionally safe.
lessonPlanData.transitions: Use target classroom language: Listen, look, stand up, sit down, work in pairs, switch roles, stop.
lessonPlanData.competencies: Oral communication; listening comprehension; interaction; alphabet awareness; classroom participation; collaboration; confidence building.
lessonPlanData.teacherNotes: Record learners needing confidence support, alphabet review, or additional listening repetition before Lesson 2.

elvyBlueprint.instructions: Smile and wave. Say Hello naturally, repeat slowly, wait, and praise any attempt. Show the greetings poster if needed.
Ask whether the learner knows Hello or Hi. Accept spoken, typed, or gesture responses and choose the pace accordingly.
Show the greetings poster. Model Hello, I’m Elvy. Nice to meet you. Build the dialogue one chunk at a time.
Ask the learner’s name. Offer I’m ____ as a frame. Recast gently and ask again when needed.
Show the classroom assets. Teach through action. Mix the order after two correct responses; model again after errors.
Show the alphabet chart. Model short groups, ask recognition first, then production. Keep the target manageable.
Remove frames gradually and ask the learner to greet and introduce themselves independently.
Show the exit ticket and assess greeting, name, one instruction, and three letters.
Give one specific praise point and one next step. Recommend review if fewer than three tasks are successful.

lessonPlanData.extraPractice: Repeat the dialogue with different names, play a home mime game, and recite the alphabet.
lessonPlanData.fastFinishers: Create two new classroom instruction cards or spell their first name to a partner.
lessonPlanData.prerequisites: No formal English prerequisite; informal exposure to greetings or letters may exist.
lessonPlanData.pronunciation: Greeting intonation; rhythm in Nice to meet you; clear alphabet letter names.
lessonPlanData.udlStrategies: Use games, personal names, partner changes, speech, print, gestures, images, movement, speaking, acting, matching, writing, and singing.
lessonPlanData.peerAssessment: Partners check that the dialogue contains a greeting, name, and polite response.
lessonPlanData.selfAssessment: Thumbs up/side/down for greeting, saying a name, following classroom English, and saying letters.

lessonPlan.theme: Greetings, introductions, classroom language, and the alphabet

stages.assessment: Observe confidence, prior knowledge, and willingness to respond.
stages.studentActivities: Respond chorally and individually and share any greeting expressions already known.
stages.teacherActivities: Smile, wave, greet the class, elicit a choral response, greet several learners individually, and diagnose prior knowledge.

stages.assessment: Recognition questions and accurate repetition.
stages.studentActivities: Look, predict, listen, identify key phrases, tick answers, and repeat.
stages.teacherActivities: Present the greeting dialogue in context, ask learners to predict, model or play it, check phrases heard, and model pronunciation and intonation.

stages.assessment: Greeting, name, polite response, and intelligibility checklist.
stages.studentActivities: Practise using personal names, switch roles, and repeat with another partner.
stages.teacherActivities: Model the complete dialogue with one learner, assign repetitions, organise pairs, require role switching, and monitor gently.

stages.assessment: Correctly perform or identify at least four instructions.
stages.studentActivities: Watch, imitate, repeat, act, match, and respond physically.
stages.teacherActivities: Teach classroom verbs and instructions using action, gesture, written forms, and mixed-order commands.

stages.assessment: Accuracy, participation, and English use.
stages.studentActivities: Mime, guess, keep score, and take turns.
stages.teacherActivities: Model and organise a mime game in groups, ensure turn-taking, and monitor equal participation.

stages.assessment: Recognition, pronunciation, and accurate recording.
stages.studentActivities: Listen, repeat, complete sequences, say chosen letters, listen to a partner, and write.
stages.teacherActivities: Display the alphabet chart, model letter names, lead a rhythm task, guide missing-letter work, and model partner dictation.

stages.assessment: Four-part exit ticket and confidence note.
stages.studentActivities: Greet, say their name, follow one instruction, and say three letters.
stages.teacherActivities: Invite an independent mini-performance and administer the exit ticket.

lessonPlan.grammar: Communicative chunks: I’m + name; My name is + name; Nice to meet you; Nice to meet you too.
lessonPlan.grouping: Whole class, pairs, groups of 3–5, and individual performance.
lessonPlan.homework: Practise the greeting dialogue with a family member and write five English alphabet letters.
lessonPlan.outcomes: Learners participate in a short greeting dialogue, demonstrate classroom routines, match classroom verbs to visuals, and complete a basic alphabet task.
lessonPlan.textbook: English Spotlight 1 — Student Book Part A
lessonPlan.functions: Greeting; introducing oneself; responding politely; following classroom instructions.
lessonPlan.resources: Student Book pages 7–10; greetings poster; classroom-language cards; instruction cards; alphabet chart; exit ticket; board.
lessonPlan.sourceBook: English Spotlight 1 Student Book Part A
lessonPlan.vocabulary: hello, hi, name, nice to meet you, listen, look, talk, speak, read, write, draw, match, point, stand up, sit down, open your book, close your book, raise your hand, work in pairs, work in groups
lessonPlan.generatedBy: Happy Office Curriculum Engineering — Elvy Pedagogy Standards
lessonPlan.teacherTips: Model every speaking task first, assign repetitions, switch roles and partners, use gestures consistently, avoid long grammar explanations, and keep the room emotionally safe.
lessonPlan.transitions: Use target classroom language: Listen, look, stand up, sit down, work in pairs, switch roles, stop.
lessonPlan.competencies: Oral communication; listening comprehension; interaction; alphabet awareness; classroom participation; collaboration; confidence building.
lessonPlan.teacherNotes: Record learners needing confidence support, alphabet review, or additional listening repetition before Lesson 2.

elvyBlueprint.instructions: Smile and wave. Say Hello naturally, repeat slowly, wait, and praise any attempt. Show the greetings poster if needed.
Ask whether the learner knows Hello or Hi. Accept spoken, typed, or gesture responses and choose the pace accordingly.
Show the greetings poster. Model Hello, I’m Elvy. Nice to meet you. Build the dialogue one chunk at a time.
Ask the learner’s name. Offer I’m ____ as a frame. Recast gently and ask again when needed.
Show the classroom assets. Teach through action. Mix the order after two correct responses; model again after errors.
Show the alphabet chart. Model short groups, ask recognition first, then production. Keep the target manageable.
Remove frames gradually and ask the learner to greet and introduce themselves independently.
Show the exit ticket and assess greeting, name, one instruction, and three letters.
Give one specific praise point and one next step. Recommend review if fewer than three tasks are successful.

lessonPlan.extraPractice: Repeat the dialogue with different names, play a home mime game, and recite the alphabet.
lessonPlan.fastFinishers: Create two new classroom instruction cards or spell their first name to a partner.
lessonPlan.prerequisites: No formal English prerequisite; informal exposure to greetings or letters may exist.
lessonPlan.pronunciation: Greeting intonation; rhythm in Nice to meet you; clear alphabet letter names.
lessonPlan.udlStrategies: Use games, personal names, partner changes, speech, print, gestures, images, movement, speaking, acting, matching, writing, and singing.
lessonPlan.peerAssessment: Partners check that the dialogue contains a greeting, name, and polite response.
lessonPlan.selfAssessment: Thumbs up/side/down for greeting, saying a name, following classroom English, and saying letters.
